production_route: D3D9 UpdateTargetFrameRate passes the configured limit to Presenter. Without present-wait, signalFrame calls FpsLimiter::delay before signaling frame latency. The existing desktop-package game logs establish the version, settings and features. The experiment compiles that source into separate timing executables.
candidate_change: On Windows the extra busy-wait margin is limited to one OS timer quantum, in addition to the existing four-quantum margin. The original adds one sixth of the requested sleep.
measurement_method: Two counterbalanced pairs per architecture. Three warm-ups for each cap precede the local QPC samples. Thread CPU is kernel plus user time from GetThreadTimes, as a percentage of one logical processor. P95 is the absolute distance from the requested interval. No graphics context or game was created by the timing program.
acceptance: This record covers the CPU timing control. The supplied app-local DXVK game binaries remain the physically accepted game configuration. The change has not been accepted for live gameplay.

observed_tradeoff.decision: Retain the existing game limiter. The bounded-spin candidate reduced measured thread CPU in every setting, but several timing tails worsened. On ARM64EC at 8 Hz, P95 absolute period error increased from 3.7164 ms to 90.2586 ms across the two short runs.
observed_tradeoff.accounting: GetThreadTimes has finite accounting granularity. One x64 group reported zero charged time despite nonzero thread-cycle counts. No system-wide CPU or power saving is inferred.

high_resolution_timer_trial.candidate_change: Use a high-resolution waitable timer owned by the calling thread. After a confirmed timer creation, cap the extra spin margin at one timer quantum. If the Windows timer cannot be created or a wait fails, use the original system wait path.
high_resolution_timer_trial.measurement_method: Two counterbalanced pairs per architecture. Three warm-ups for each cap precede the local QPC samples. Thread CPU is kernel plus user time from GetThreadTimes, as a percentage of one logical processor. P95 is the absolute distance from the requested interval. No graphics context or game was created by the timing program.
high_resolution_timer_trial.probe_logging: The two timing builds increment one per-thread test counter after each completed blocking wait. The production patch excludes these counters. Waits inside the spin loop are not instrumented.
high_resolution_timer_trial.decision: The first recorded period in each old run includes setup outside the uninterrupted return-to-return window. The boundary correction below supersedes the original tail comparison; CPU time is aggregated over the original wall windows.

contiguous_boundary_correction.method: Each run allocated its timestamp array and queried thread accounting after the last warmup return. Exclude the first non-contiguous interval symmetrically. Original input rows are unchanged.

x86_three_way_30_60.scope: CPU-only actual DXVK limiter returns; thread CPU aggregate and QPC. The game and its frame presentation are measured separately. GetThreadTimes CPU accounting is quantized; per-run cycles are included.

instrumentation.sampling: Store timestamps on return from 241 consecutive limiter calls to delimit 240 intervals. Query CPU and cycle counters once outside the frame interval array, run each side twice in the order reference, high-resolution, fixed500, fixed500, high-resolution, reference.

x86_three_way_30_60.time_accounting: At 60 Hz the fixed-tail thread reported zero GetThreadTimes ticks in both 4-second windows, with nonzero thread cycles. Reported zero is below this measurement resolution. Tail latency worsened on both caps. No game or battery savings were qualified.

actual_game.first_private_run: The high-integrity process ignored the child-only ICD environment variable. Both an ordinary registered-app loader query and a direct ICD query matched the native LUID; the private application paths required explicit selection.
actual_game.evidence: Original desktop DLL opened the 320x240 D3D9 window. FTE logged GM20B, renderer initialization and client connection. A subsequent unexpected boot interrupted the warmup before durable map/input/measurement/exit acceptance.
